$schema_note: Physical-roof audit of every pre-existing (non-recon_*) 1835 structure record. inventory_roof_count is the number deducted from the 665-roof programme; attached ranges remain one inventory roof unless the source describes distinct buildings.

method.eligible: A covered building or independently roofed working structure plausibly standing on the scene date.
method.ineligible: Open ground/enclosure, bridge, pier, incomplete roofless works, or a building whose July existence is contradicted by the production chronology.
method.compound: roof_count records distinct physical roof masses; inventory_roof_count counts attached ranges as one roofed building but counts separately described cabins separately.
method.substitution: Each eligible existing inventory roof explicitly replaces that many anonymous programme slots in its district/family; it is not added above 665.

T-0883. One gable roof on the garrison's barn, placed off the 1830 Harrison plan and corroborated in position by Hubbard. A2 (barn or carriage shed) IS READ OFF THE FUNCTION AND NOT THE BAND: 47 x 31 ft stands above A2's 18-26 by 28-44 ft on both axes, which is what a plate that calls a building BIG should produce, and no wider family fits a barn. THE FORT COLUMN IS FULL AND THIS ROOF IS NOT IN IT. The inventory's district matrix authorises ten roofs in the fort district, all of them under fort_principal, and ten stand — this building is the eleventh, twelfth or thirteenth. It substitutes no anonymous slot and the zero is deliberate: the fort column's own text says 'ten principal roofs in the custom Fort Dearborn compound', and these three are service buildings on the reservation OUTSIDE the pickets, which that sentence never counted. They are additions above the district's estimate, which is what the programme file's exceedance report exists to report.

T-0881. One gable roof on the larger of the two blocks the 1830 Harrison plan letters `Out Buildings` — plural, and drawn twice, which is the correction this ticket made to its own premise. A5 (small utility) IS CHOSEN BECAUSE IT NAMES NO USE, which is the record's own position: `Out buildings` says what a building is not, and a post's out buildings are privies, wood sheds, stores and pens. 24 x 19 ft sits just above A5's 6-8 by 12-16 ft band; the family is taken anyway, because a family label here is a roof-counting convenience and a use would be a claim. Confidence is low and not moderate: one witness, pre-1835 by five years, and no second source mentions these buildings at all. THE FORT COLUMN IS FULL AND THIS ROOF IS NOT IN IT. The inventory's district matrix authorises ten roofs in the fort district, all of them under fort_principal, and ten stand — this building is one more above them, exactly as the three service buildings T-0883 added are. T-1036. One gable roof on the United States factory, 152 m south of the pickets, where the 1830 Harrison plan letters `U.S. Factor's House` against three blocks and this record builds the one the label touches. C2 (store-residence) IS CHOSEN BECAUSE IT NAMES WHAT A FACTORY WAS AND NOTHING MORE — the government's trading house, a shop and a dwelling in one building — and because it is the only family in the crosswalk that puts trade and living under one roof without naming a trade. THE BAND DOES NOT FIT AND THE FAMILY IS TAKEN ANYWAY: 67 x 26 ft is far outside C2's 18x30-22x40 ft and its 1.5 levels against this building's two, exactly as W4's band does not fit the shop and A5's does not fit out building (a). F2 (narrow two-storey warehouse, 20x40-26x60 ft, two levels) fits the numbers much better and was refused on the label: a warehouse is a use, this building is attested as a factor's HOUSE with a family living in it from 1822, and a family label here is a roof-counting convenience while a use would be a claim. Confidence is low: the roof itself is invented (L231), and the building's own witnesses say nothing about it. THE FORT COLUMN IS FULL AND THIS ROOF IS NOT IN IT. The inventory's district matrix authorises ten roofs in the fort district, all under fort_principal, and ten stand — this is one more above them, on the same footing as the three service buildings T-0883 added and the two out buildings T-0881 added. It substitutes no anonymous slot and the zero is deliberate: the fort column's own text says 'ten principal roofs in the custom Fort Dearborn compound', and this building stands on the reservation OUTSIDE the pickets, which that sentence never counted. It is an addition above the district's estimate, which is what the programme file's exceedance report exists to report.

Documented two-story frame inn on Lake Street near Wells, one principal roof — the same reading as tremont_house_1 and exchange_coffee_house. Andreas p. 635 has it built in 1834 and opened by Johnson and Stevens, and the Chicago American of 13 June 1835 advertises two professional offices in it seventeen days before the scene date, so it is a covered building standing on 1 July 1835 and eligible. It is a PRE-EXISTING roof, not a reconstructed one: the town this project models already had it, so it substitutes an anonymous T2 slot rather than adding to the target. T2 is the frontier-inn family — two storeys, clapboard frame, 5-8 bays — which is what Andreas's 'two-story building, with eaves to the street' describes; T1 is the lower one-and-a-half-storey public house and T3 is the Sauganash's single custom asset, and neither fits. No stable is attested here, so no A1 roof is claimed with it (T2's own crosswalk note forbids adding one silently).

T-0133. A reconstructed freight shed on the north bank at the Dearborn crossing, built from image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18 ('low warehouses on the banks'). It is an eligible physical roof and it is counted as one, in the north district under family F1 (freight or storage shed). IT SUBSTITUTES NO ANONYMOUS SLOT AND THE FIGURE IS ZERO ON PURPOSE: the inventory's district matrix allows the north division ONE warehouse-or-freight roof and the Kinzie and Hunter forwarding store already stands on it, so there is no north freight slot for this roof to replace. It is therefore an addition above the district's estimate rather than a substitution inside it, which is what the plate asks for and what the programme file's own exceedance report is for.
